title: Structural Theorems for de Sitter-Unruh Modified Inertia: What the First-Moment Closure Forbids
description:
v3 changes the kernel. v1–v2 stated every result for K(z)=(√(1+4z)−1)/(2√z), the α=1 class. v3 adopts an α≥2 kernel, K(z)=√(z/(1+z)), because α=1 forces a constant sunward anomaly a0/2 that is 1279× the Earth 2σ ephemeris bound (Sereno & Jetzer 2006) and drives the companion disformal lensing construction's own B<1 premise past 257× across Mercury→Saturn, while buying only +0.0033 dex on 175 SPARC galaxies (0.10σint).

a0 = cHΛ/Z is unaffected. Every premise the coefficient's derivation uses — Herglotz–Nevanlinna positivity, passivity sup K = 1, the unit sum rule ∫dμ/|t| = K(∞)−K(0) = 1, the horizon floor — holds for the new kernel, which also keeps the deep-MOND √z origin. What is withdrawn is the word ‘exact’: the relation gobs² = gbar² + a0gbar is an α=1 identity and is no longer claimed.

All seven results survive. Three carry new numbers, one falsifier is qualified, and there is one new result — the α=2 spectral measure ρ(s) = (1/π)√(s/(1−s)) on 0<s<1, derived in closed form by Stieltjes inversion and verified against the closed form to 8×10−15 over eight decades. It is strictly simpler than v2's: one spectral region instead of two, compact support instead of unbounded, finite total mass 1/2 instead of divergent, and no additive constant. The divergence was the problem — an unbounded measure is exactly what produces the α=1 tail.

Changed: the acceleration Hessian determinant (−3√2/64 = −0.06629, still non-singular, so Theorem 3 stands); the linear-response inertia h(x) = x(x²+2)/(1+x²)3/2 (its deep limit 1/h → 1/(2x) is identical to v2's, so every deep-regime application is unaffected); the rotation-curve dipole (5.4–15.4% at e<<y, 1.10× v2's). Qualified: v2 claimed the dipole's sign ‘is forced by the cross term and cannot be tuned’; under α=2 the sign flips in the e>>y corner, at sub-0.2% amplitude, so the >1% falsifier is unaffected but the sign is forced only for e≲y. Unchanged: Theorems 1 and 4 (kinematic); Theorem 2 (the branch cut moves from z≤−1/4 to −1<z<0 and becomes compact, but the disjointness argument is identical); Proposition 7's offset (−0.0369 dex against v2's −0.037).

The verification script reproduces both published v2 values first — the Hessian −11/25+23√5/125 and the Prop-7 offset −0.037 dex, by v2's own method — as a machinery check, so every change is attributable to the kernel and not to the author. v2's retraction of Proposition 7's observational forecast still stands.

Credit. The interpolating function is Milgrom's (1983) ‘standard’ μ; v1–v2's was Milgrom (1999), whose dS–Unruh derivation also fixes the coefficient at 2cHΛ. Neither kernel is original here. The distinctive content is the cHΛ/Z coefficient and the modified-inertia completion. κ=½ and Z remain postulated; this is a one-parameter effective theory. Both a0 footings (9.36×10−11 and 1.13×10−10 m s−2) are carried throughout.
notes:
VERSION 2 -- SELF-CORRECTION AFTER A REAL-DATA CONFRONTATION. v1's Proposition 7 attached an observational forecast to its two propositions: '~1.2-1.9 sigma on 40-60 Local Group dwarfs, 3 sigma at N~150, both routes archival'. THAT FORECAST WAS WRONG AND IS RETRACTED IN v2. Running the test on the real McConnachie (2012) catalogue (VizieR J/AJ/144/4/catalog, 46 of 102 usable rows) shows it is SYSTEMATICS-LIMITED, not sample-limited: per-object scatter is 0.38-0.48 dex rather than the assumed 0.15-0.20, and the dominant error -- the stellar mass-to-light ratio -- is COHERENT across the sample, so sqrt(N) does not reduce it. Varying Upsilon_V over 1-4 moves the mean residual by 0.322 dex, 8.7x the 0.037 dex signal; matching the signal would need Upsilon_V to 19% against a literature spread of 50-100%. Propositions 7.1 and 7.2 are UNCHANGED -- a theorem and a calculation -- and Theorems 1-5 and Proposition 6 are untouched. Only the forecast built on Prop 7 fails. New Sections 9.1-9.2 give the real-catalogue confrontation and the one surviving route: the Upsilon direction has a -0.067/dex slope against log(g_bar/a0) while the closure offset is flat, so the two are partially separable over the 5.28 dex of dynamic range available -- which requires the closure offset computed ACROSS g_bar, not done here.

Five of the seven results SUBTRACT from the framework: they remove a postulate, a channel, a class of actions, and a cosmological sector from its reach. Two prior claims in the author's own corpus are retracted here: that pure modified inertia predicts exactly zero directional asymmetry (Theorem 5), and the treatment of the sign as a parameter awaiting data (Corollary 2.2). The moment-identity-versus-Euler-Lagrange gap of Section 5 is recorded as unresolved, the MOND saddle region of Section 7 as outside the validity of the point-particle treatment, and the Section 9 orbit calculation as planar and idealised. v3 (2026-07-30): kernel changed from alpha=1 to alpha>=2; new spectral measure derived; the word 'exact' withdrawn from the algebraic relation; all seven results survive, three with new numbers and one falsifier qualified. Supersedes v2 (10.5281/zenodo.21708842). v4 (2026-07-30): file-set fix only -- v3 inadvertently dropped PROVENANCE.md and mcconnachie2012_dsph.csv, the data and extraction record behind section 9.1. No scientific content differs from v3.
